title: Per-service Flyway history table name and migration-run record fields are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 section R4 and R5.5 DP-15; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29; legacy story RWB-E1-044 sections 11, 12 and 13
description: The as-built story names one history table, flyway_schema_history_recovery, and one Job response for the run record. The target rule is one Flyway sequence per service in the service's own schema, but no source document gives the history table name that a service uses, whether it keeps the Flyway default flyway_schema_history or a per-service name, or the exact field list of the migration-run record that each service writes to the P1 job view. The preserved story keeps the as-built table and points at the delta stories, so a build team cannot name the table or the record fields from the documents alone.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-15 names the per-service sequence but not the table; Architecture v5 slide 29 says each service runs its own Flyway migrations without naming a history table; the only named table in the sources is the as-built flyway_schema_history_recovery
proposed: Fix the history table name (Flyway default flyway_schema_history in the service's own schema) and the migration-run record fields in RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, and keep the as-built flyway_schema_history_recovery only in the preserved RWB-PLT-E1044-APP

title: Baseline order and sequence start across the 19 services are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-15; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29 and 41; legacy story RWB-E1-044 section 13 (D-RCV-28 build rule)
description: Each service gets one V0001 baseline, but no source document states the order in which the 19 baselines are created, whether the four-digit sequence restarts at V0001 in every service or continues from one number, or how a migration that must run before another service's baseline is ordered. The migration-run record fields are open in the same way: the legacy Job response is the only shape, and the target record must say which service and which schema a run belongs to.
evidence: Legacy story RWB-E1-044 section 13 fixes V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql for the single recovery schema and says the four-digit sequence is taken in merge order; Architecture v5 slide 29 says Flyway per service in its own pipeline but gives no cross-service order; no document names the sequence start per service
proposed: State in RWB-PLT-E1044-CON that every service starts at V0001 in its own folder and that baselines have no cross-service order, and publish the run-record fields with the service and schema keys

title: Contract artefact location and owner of the Flyway configuration module are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 section R4 and section R8.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 and slide 38 (service template in wave 0); legacy story RWB-E1-044 sections 12 and 13
description: The migration contract is one document shared by 19 services, but no source document gives its location, its file name or whether it lives in the platform template repository or in each service repository. The same is true of the Flyway configuration module: the as-built story put it in the recovery module (recovery.casewf.migration), while the target template is a shared platform artefact, and no document says whether the platform template owns the Flyway module and each service only supplies its folder and baseline, or each service owns its own module.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 29 says Flyway per service in its own pipeline; slide 38 lists the service template as a wave 0 platform item; legacy story RWB-E1-044 section 13 names the package recovery.casewf.migration with no target equivalent; no source names the contract document path or its owner
proposed: Publish the contract document in the platform template repository next to the Flyway module, name the platform template as the owner of the module, and keep only the migration folder and the V0001 baseline in each service

title: Job-run record fields, alert threshold and owner of the drift feature flag after the split are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 section R3 default rulings (feature flags: platform library); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 33 (two deployments per service); legacy story RWB-E1-044 section 13 (feature flag rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate) and section 12 (migration job output)
section: Data; Solution plan; Screens and states
description: The deployment writes one job-run record per service and raises one alert on a failed run, but no source document gives the record field list as a deployment contract, the alert threshold (how many failed runs, over what window, to which channel) or who owns the legacy feature flag rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate once the monolith module is split into 19 services and the platform template. The legacy flag name and its values (on in SIT, UAT and PROD, off in DEV) are the only fixed facts.
evidence: Legacy story RWB-E1-044 section 13 gives the flag name and values only; section 12 gives a Job output row without a field list; Template and Rules v1 section R3 gives the platform library as the owner of feature flags by default ruling but not for this flag after the split
proposed: Publish the job-run record fields in RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, fix one alert per failed run per service in RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS, and assign the flag rwb.p3.migration-drift-gate to the platform library owner with the legacy values unchanged

title: The chart name and registry, the resource sizes, the KEDA thresholds, the toolchain, the promotion gates and the chart version scheme are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5 (DP-15), R7.2 s12 and R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 29, 33, 38, 41 and 48; Business Requirements Program v4 section 6.9 (NFR-052, NFR-054); WP B-PLT-TPL-01 story line RWB-PLT-N004-OPS
section: 3 Preconditions; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.9 Call-type summary; 13 Solution plan
description: No source read fixes the name of the one Helm chart and the name of the chart repository that holds it, the container registry and the image naming a values file points at, the requests and limits of the api and worker tiers, the KEDA ceiling and backlog threshold per service, the CI toolchain that runs the template and its scanners, the promotion gates and the roles that approve each environment, or the chart version scheme and the pinning format a service repository uses.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 38 names 'service template + Helm', 'one Helm chart' and 'golden pipeline' as wave 0 items but gives no name, repository, registry, version scheme or toolchain; slides 33 and 48 fix the api at 2 small pods and the worker as 0 to many by KEDA with no pod size or threshold; slide 20 fixes /health and /metrics with no port; R4 fixes the schema, topic, queue and REST base shapes but no chart or image name; NFR-052 and NFR-054 state the secret and pipeline-blocking rules with no tool, stage or gate named; ownership.json names PLT as the owner of the outbox, inbox and idempotency library tables and of the outbox relay JOB-11, and names no chart, registry, pipeline or promotion approver.
proposed: Publish the chart name, the chart repository and the registry and image naming, the api and worker resource defaults with the per-service overrides each service OPS story fills in, the KEDA ceiling and backlog threshold per service, the CI toolchain and its scanner set, the promotion gate and approver role of each of DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD, and the chart and template version scheme with the pinning format; confirm both assumptions with the platform administrator and the DevOps lead before the chart is Published and before the canary runs.

title: The NF-01 legacy story text, the exact repository layout, the branch policy, the toolchain and the template version scheme are not in the source set
source: _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json (key NF-01: title only, no story_file, no acs, no tcs, no reqs, no sections); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 4, 20, 29, 33, 38 and 41; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md NFR-045, NFR-052 and NFR-054 (§6 and §7 constraint Built on ACE); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15 and §R9
section: 2 Business rationale (last-but-two paragraph); 3 Preconditions; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: No source in the set states the NF-01 legacy story text or any of its acceptance criteria, test cases, messages or sections: the legacy index entry holds the title Repository and pipeline baseline, the group NF and empty metadata, requirements, acceptance criteria, test cases, messages and sections, and there is no story file behind it, so nothing is preserved and no AC or TC is inherited. The baseline that replaces it is derived from Arch v5 slides 4, 20, 29, 33, 38 and 41 and from NFR-045, NFR-052 and NFR-054, and no source fixes the five delivery choices that a repository baseline has to fix: the exact layout inside the six folders api, worker, db/migration, contracts, helm and pipeline; the branch policy, protected-branch setting and release tag convention; the toolchain (build tool, CI engine, artefact registry, image registry and the three scanner products); the template version scheme and the file in which a repository pins it; and the repository naming convention beyond a derivation from the §R4 short name. The story can be stated and tested against an assumption for each, but a service team cannot create its repository from the story alone, and a template upgrade cannot be audited, until the five are published.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 4 gives the rule one deployable service per module with its own code, release, owner, contract, schema, topic and task queue, slides 20 and 33 give the shape every service shares, slide 38 makes the service template and the golden pipeline wave-0 enablers and slide 41 gives the naming of schema, REST base, topic and task queue, but none of them names a repository layout, a branch policy, a toolchain or a version scheme; slide 29 fixes the schema boundary by grant but not the build-time check that this story adds; NFR-045, NFR-052 and NFR-054 fix what a repository must not contain but not how the scan is configured. The legacy index entry for NF-01 (chars 0, status empty, story_file null) and the absence of an NF-01 story file in 04 User stories confirm that the legacy text cannot fill any of the five.
proposed: Publish the NF-01 legacy story text into the source set and confirm the repository layout inside each folder, the branch policy, the toolchain and the template version scheme at the wave 0 entry check, then restate AC1 to AC5 against the published text; until then the baseline runs on ASM-B-PLT-TPL-01-NF01-1 to ASM-B-PLT-TPL-01-NF01-5 and the five are treated as values of the template.

title: The legacy NF-03 story text is absent from the source set, and the hosts, subscriptions, sizing, data refresh cadence and environment owners of the four environments are stated nowhere
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 8, 23, 24, 29, 33, 38 and 41); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md (NFR-045 and NFR-052); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json (NF-03 entry)
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 1, 2 and 9; 10 Authority; 11 Data (environment matrix, values that differ, data classes); 13 Solution plan (Done when); 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy index entry for NF-03 holds only the key, the title Environment baseline, the group NF and empty metadata, requirements, acceptance criteria, test cases, messages and sections, and no story file behind it, so no legacy acceptance criterion, test case or section can be preserved or copied. The environment baseline is therefore derived from Architecture v5 slides 8, 23, 24, 29, 33, 38 and 41 and from NFR-045 and NFR-052. Those sources fix the shape of each environment, one Temporal cluster per environment with its own persistence database and the namespace rwb-recovery, codec keys in Key Vault per namespace, one schema and one login per service in the ACE database with one PgBouncer pool and connection cap per login, and the data classes of development, user acceptance and production, but they state no environment host or URL, no subscription or resource group, no region pairing beyond the agreed Southeast Asia tenancy, no sizing of a Temporal cluster, of an ACE database or of a pool, no connection cap, no replica count, no data refresh cadence for development, system integration or user acceptance, no owner role per environment and no approver role for a promotion.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 23 gives one Temporal cluster per environment on ACE AKS with its own persistence database, UI, metrics and codec server and version 1.30 or later, and a namespace per workbench with its own retention, quotas, certificates and codec keys, but names no host, size or owner. Slide 24 repeats one cluster per environment with a queue per service and codec keys in Key Vault per namespace, and gives no environment name beyond the phrase per environment. Slide 29 gives one ACE database, 19 schemas and 19 logins, one PgBouncer pool with a connection cap and a statement timeout per login, and Temporal persistence in its own database, but no cap value, no pool size and no host. Slide 8 places the 19 services in the shared ACE AKS cluster behind the shared App Gateway and gives no environment list. Slide 38 makes the chart, the 19 schemas and logins and Temporal 1.30 or later Wave 0 work and gives no environment. Slide 41 gives the naming rule per service and no environment value. NFR-045 fixes synthetic data in development and masked copies in user acceptance and names no cadence, no retention and no owner. NFR-052 fixes that secrets live in the key store and names no key store, no subscription and no rotation. The legacy index entry for NF-03 carries empty meta, reqs, acs, tcs, msgs and sections and a null story file, so the legacy story itself cannot supply any of these values either.
proposed: Agree the environment pack with the platform administrator and the solution architect before the first promotion is taken as the run of record: the four rows DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD on the shared ACE AKS cluster and the shared App Gateway with their hosts and ingress hosts, the subscription, resource group and region of each, the Temporal cluster and persistence database of each with its size, the namespace rwb-recovery in each with its key store and codec key naming, the ACE database server of each with the 19 logins, the PgBouncer pool and connection cap per login, the API and worker replica counts, the data refresh cadence and source of development, system integration and user acceptance, the owner role of each environment and the approver role of the promotion gate, all held as values in the environment matrix of the platform repository.

title: The NF-04 legacy story text is absent, and the key-store naming, rotation values, secret owners and configuration key names are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.3 and R9; _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json NF-04 entry (title only, every other field empty); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 20, 24, 29 and 35; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 NFR-052, NFR-054 and REQ-DRI-010; ownership.json (no key store, no configuration key naming, no rotation value)
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: No source read gives the NF-04 legacy story text, so the baseline has no legacy acceptance criteria, test cases or requirements to inherit and is derived from the slides and the three requirements. No source read gives the Key Vault name, the key-store object path convention per service, the rotation interval per secret family, the overlap window before the previous version is disabled, the secret owner role per family beyond the platform administrator, the configuration key names of the non-secret environment settings, the scanner products of the pipeline gate, the approved-dependency list, or the form and length of a secret reference.
evidence: The NF-04 row of the legacy index carries title "Secrets and configuration baseline" with meta, module, release, requirements, acceptance criteria, test cases, messages, sections, status and story file all empty; NFR-052 and NFR-054 give the rule and the target ("No secrets in code or prompts", "Pipeline checks pass") and no value; REQ-DRI-010 gives the parameter catalog and the configuration service and no key names; Arch v5 slides 8, 20 and 24 name the Key Vault and the per-namespace codec keys and give no object naming or rotation value; and the ownership map lists no key store and no configuration key.
proposed: Publish the Key Vault naming and the object path convention, the rotation interval and the overlap window per secret family, the secret owner role per family, the configuration key naming of the non-secret settings, the scanner products and the approved-dependency list, and the form of a secret reference, at the wave 0 entry check with the platform administrator and the security architect; a value that is still open is carried as a configuration value so that closing it needs no code change.
